claims.text: Equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness and strength in its disordered solid-solution state.
The disordered CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has minimal local lattice distortions.
The disordered CoCrFeNiTi solid solution lacks significant short-range order.
Minimal lattice distortion and the absence of significant short-range order produce highly mobile dislocation networks.
Weak dislocation pinning permits easy dislocation motion in the untreated alloy.
Easy dislocation motion promotes high ductility and machinability.
Easy dislocation motion limits hardness and strength.
The applicable starting material is a single-phase, disordered solid solution of equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
A controlled thermomechanical treatment can induce short-range order or fine precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi.
Minimal atomic-size mismatch and weak long-range interactions in the as-cast state lead to low lattice friction.
Short-range order increases local stress fields that pin dislocations.
Fine precipitates increase local stress fields that pin dislocations.
Thermomechanically induced short-range order or precipitates will increase yield strength relative to the untreated state.
Thermomechanically induced short-range order or precipitates will increase hardness relative to the untreated state.
The strengthening treatment will reduce ductility relative to the untreated state.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to room-temperature, quasi-static tensile or compressive loading.
